text:
Artyom Levshunov was the second pick in 2024, right after Macklin Celebrini, and the Blackhawks are giving him the minutes that come with that: 20 and a half a night at 21 years old. The points have not come. He has three in 25 games, 0.12 a game, where the defensemen taken in the top four since 2005 typically scored about 0.36 in their first full season.

Some of that is the team around him. Chicago has scored 4.7 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, which costs a defenseman assists, and that usually swings back. Evolving-Hockey noted last season that he plays with some of the weakest teammates in the league.

The rest is real, and it's the part to watch. At five on five the Blackhawks get only 40% of the expected goals with him out there, and Evolving-Hockey had opponents creating more against him last season than against almost any defenseman. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking sees nothing far from typical in his nine tracked games this season, nothing clear yet. For a player this young, the defensive numbers moving matters more than the point total.
headline: Levshunov's hard first full season
